newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Miners worsen gold price sale impact - RBA chief.
newsitem.headline: Miners worsen gold price sale impact - RBA chief.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane, defending the bank's recent gold sales, has accused miners of exaggerating the price impact of the sale.
In an interview with The Australian newspaper, Macfarlane said the mining industry was "not helping the price by keeping these issues in the headlines every day".
The normally media-shy governor defended the sale as in the national interest, saying it would earn taxpayers about an extra A$150 million a year.
World gold prices slumped to 12-year lows after the RBA announced on July 3 that it had sold two thirds of its reserves.
The RBA, which reduced its holdings from 247 tonnes to 80 tonnes over the last six months, said it would invest the proceeds from the sale in foreign currency assets like bonds.
The sale has been widely condemned by the gold industry, with one senior miner on Thursday questioning the wisdom of having an independent central bank.
In his interview, Macfarlane said the bank often had to take decisions in the national interest which hurt sectoral groups.
"If we raise interest rates, the housing sector is the first to complain; if the exchange rate rises, it's usually the farmers and miners. We have to live with this," he said.
"I think they (miners) somewhat exaggerate our impact on the overall world market," the paper quoted Macfarlane as saying.
"Heavy forward selling by producers has not helped either," the RBA governor added.
He said the gold price had been heavily influenced over the past year by European central bank sales and by proposals by the International Monetary Fund to sell gold to fund debt relief.
He also cited a research paper from the US Federal Reserve which proposed the US central bank sell down its gold reserves.
Macfarlane said the gold sale decision was taken by the RBA board, not the government. Sydney newsroom -- 61-2 9373-1800
